title: Is photographic memory a real thing?
summary: Josh and Chuck examine whether photographic memory is real. They conclude that perfect, flawless photographic recall does not exist, though some people have exceptional memories. They cover eidetic memory in children aged roughly six to twelve, including the Nazi-era studies and the trance-like state, and the hosts' hypotheses about language development. They discuss how the photographic memory myth persists, plagiarism accusations against author Kaavya Viswanathan, memory sports and competitions (including the World Memory Championship and Dominic O'Brien), memory palaces, synesthesia (Solomon Shereshevsky), savant-like figures (Kim Peek, John von Neumann, Stephen Wiltshire), and hyperthymesia (Jill Price). They also cover Charles Stromeyer's random-dot tests, his wife Elizabeth, and John Merritt's identics test. The episode ends with a listener email about mental health.

segments.title: Tour dates and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh announces upcoming SYSK Live tour dates, then the hosts banter about being in an elementary-school-like setting and introduce the topic of photographic memory, which they say is not real.

segments.title: Photographic memory is not real
segments.summary: The hosts argue that people claiming photographic memory are overstating a better-than-average memory. Perfect, flawless recall does not exist, and even gifted rememberers make errors.

segments.title: Eidetic memory in children
segments.summary: Eidetic memory (idetic memory) is described as found in children roughly six to twelve. Subjects view an image and describe it in present tense, holding it in their line of sight. Blinking or speaking breaks the effect, and errors occur.

segments.title: Nazi studies and the history of eidetic research
segments.summary: The hosts say Nazi researchers were among the earliest to study eidetic memory and used it for propaganda about Aryan superiority, which gave the field a bad reputation. Research then lapsed for decades. Hypotheses link the phenomenon's disappearance after age twelve to language development and labeling.

segments.title: Why the myth persists: plagiarism, memory sports and memory techniques
segments.summary: Myths about geniuses having photographic memory persist. Kaavya Viswanathan claimed photographic memory in response to plagiarism accusations. The hosts describe mind sports, including memory, mind mapping, speed reading, IQ and creative thinking, and the World Memory Championship in Wuhan, China. Dominic O'Brien describes memory as technique and practice, and memory palaces are explained.

segments.title: Synesthesia, obsession, and savant memory
segments.summary: Solomon Shereshevsky is described as a synesthete whose associations aided his memory. Relentless obsession is linked to the Shas Pollock, who memorized the Babylonian Talmud. John von Neumann is described as a mathematical genius with specific memory strengths. Stephen Wiltshire is discussed as an artist rather than a photographic-memory example.

segments.title: Kim Peek and Jill Price (hyperthymesia)
segments.summary: Kim Peek, the inspiration for Rain Man, is described for his calendar and phone-book memory and his brain structure without a corpus callosum. Jill Price is discussed as having hyperthymesia (HSAM), which is autobiographical rather than semantic memory, and linked possibly to OCD. The hosts discuss the emotional burden of not forgetting and Mary Lou Henner as an opposite example.

segments.title: Charles Stromeyer, Elizabeth and random dot tests
segments.summary: Charles Stromeyer ran newspaper-ad random-dot memory tests at Harvard in the 1970s. He found a woman named Elizabeth who appeared able to combine two dot layers in memory, and he married her. John Merritt later showed the test identifies eidetikers, not photographic memory, and the hosts mention testing with don't-blink instructions.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: A listener named Georgia writes about how the show helped with mental illness. The hosts thank her and sign off with contact and podcast network info.
